target_customer: Pharma and biotech companies, especially cell and gene therapy makers, that need scalable manufacturing capacity
problem: Individualized drugs and cell therapies are made by hand, which is slow, costly and hard to scale.
business_model: Robotics as a service: sells robotic production capacity deployed in customer facilities

founders.name: Fred Parietti
education: MIT trained roboticist per one report

founders.name: Alice Melocchi
founders.background_notes: Pharmaceutical science background not detailed by sources found.

competitors.name: ARxIUM (RIVA)
competitors.what: IV compounding robots for hospital pharmacies
competitors.traction_then: RIVA prepared over 10 million doses by 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Sterile robotic systems for GMP biologics manufacturing with regulatory compliance and cloud control are hardware, software and regulatory heavy.

defensibility.rationale: Validated GMP systems embedded in customers' facilities are slow and costly to replace or replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent pharmacy compounding robots targeted a different workflow; no sources show them copying cell therapy robotics.

market_need_then: Rising pipelines of individualized therapies, especially cell therapies, outpaced manual manufacturing capacity; later pharma partners validated this.

identity.visual_style: Playful icons and team photos, formal and fun versions
identity.voice_and_tone: Bold and forward looking, short punchy headlines like Closed. Automated. Scalable.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct internal culture language, but search shows confusion with unrelated companies named Multiply and no press on the brand itself.

pivots.from: Robotic capsule production for individualized drugs
pivots.to: Robotic manufacturing of cell and gene therapies, then wider biologics
pivots.why: Platform later expanded beyond cell and gene therapy per Series B coverage; the timing of the earlier shift is not sourced

outcome_analysis: Multiply Labs is a hardware heavy robotics company that moved from individualized drug production into robotic cell therapy manufacturing. It raised a 20M Series A in 2021, partnered with AstraZeneca and NVIDIA by early 2026 and raised a 75M Series B led by NantWorks. A hard technical and regulatory moat plus pharma partnerships support its position, but commercial scale is still unproven.
notes: Series B date October 2026 comes from an aggregator snippet; the press articles agree on 75M and NantWorks but the search did not show their publication date, so the date is unverified. A search result mentions an 85M deal with Retro Bio, not recorded as a round. Total funding figures from Tracxn and Tryfundable conflict and are unverified. Competitors listed are adjacent pharmacy robotics; no direct 2016 cell therapy automation competitor found with a dated source. Several aggregator pages wrongly describe the company as a capsule maker. Series A investors beyond Casdin Capital not confirmed. The pivot entry is tentative.
